incidents.victim: Romania — National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration (ANCPI)
incidents.vector: Attacker logged in with valid stolen credentials, mapped internal systems, then wiped servers and backups after a failed extortion attempt.
incidents.impact: Romania's entire digital land registry and e-Terra platform were knocked offline for over a week, halting property transactions nationwide, while employee credentials and e-Terra source code were exfiltrated and offered for sale. Officials are rebuilding the network from an offline backup; the actor ('ByteToBreach') is alleged to be based in Oran, Algeria.

incidents.victim: WordPress websites (tens of millions of default installs)
incidents.vector: Attackers chain an unauthenticated SQL injection (CVE-2026-60137) with a WordPress Batch REST API logic flaw (CVE-2026-63030) to achieve remote code execution on default installs.
incidents.impact: Within days of the July 17 'WP2Shell' disclosure, honeypots logged tens of thousands of exploit attempts and 100+ attacker-created admin backdoors, with threat actors deploying fake plugins and RATs such as Overlord. WordPress 7.0.2 patches both flaws and forced auto-updates were enabled.

incidents.victim: Craneware (billing/pharmacy software provider to 2,000+ US hospitals)
incidents.vector: Intruders gained unauthorized access to a subset of Craneware's data environment and copied a large number of files.
incidents.impact: Employee, customer and business-partner records were stolen from the Edinburgh-based hospital software vendor; the intrusion is contained and hospital services were not disrupted. The scope of stolen data, including any patient information, is still being determined.

incidents.victim: South Korea — Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Korea National Diplomatic Academy)
incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a previously unknown zero-day in the diplomatic academy's e-learning server software, compounded by misconfigured security settings.
incidents.impact: Hackers had access to the academy's online training platform for roughly nine months (Apr 2025–Feb 2026), stealing IDs, names, emails and encrypted passwords of current and former ministry personnel. Seoul did not attribute the attack but ascribes ~80% of state-sector intrusions to North Korea.

incidents.victim: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant contractor (Reliance Infrastructure), India
incidents.vector: Extortion group breached a Reliance Infrastructure server hosted at data-center provider Yotta — possibly via exposed RDP, phishing or a Fortinet flaw — and published stolen files after non-payment.
incidents.impact: About 19,000 files (14.3 GB) tied to non-nuclear 'balance of plant' construction for Kudankulam Units 3 and 4 were leaked by the World Leaks group. India's nuclear operator said the documents relate only to conventional support facilities and pose no nuclear safety or security risk.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack reached Fairlife production-related systems; the initial access vector was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Coca-Cola suspended production at Fairlife's US factories after hackers accessed production systems, per an SEC filing; Canadian production lines were unaffected and no ransomware group has yet claimed the attack.

incidents.vector: Data theft via the Oracle E-Business Suite mass-exploitation campaign attributed to the Clop group.
incidents.impact: Estée Lauder confirmed customer data was stolen from its Oracle EBS platform in last year's Clop hacking spree, disclosing to US state regulators nearly a year after the incident. It is the cosmetics firm's second breach since 2023.

incidents.vector: An autonomous AI agent exploited a code-execution flaw in the platform's data-processing pipeline via a malicious dataset, then pivoted into internal systems.
incidents.impact: Attackers harvested internal datasets and cloud/cluster credentials; Hugging Face says no customer data was exposed and advised users to rotate access tokens. Notably, its own frontier-model incident analysis was blocked by the model's abuse guardrails.

incidents.vector: Intrusion linked by security firm Expel to a China-based, financially motivated operation.
incidents.impact: Expel tied a breach of certificate authority DigiCert to a financially motivated China-based subgroup, raising concerns about trust-infrastructure compromise. Full scope was not detailed.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social-engineering lures trigger WebDAV/MSHTA-delivered PowerShell and Python loaders — some using blockchain 'EtherHiding' for C2 — to run ACR Stealer in memory.
incidents.impact: Microsoft observed rising ACR Stealer activity (late Apr–mid-Jun 2026) stealing browser credentials, session tokens and enterprise documents, enabling account compromise and follow-on intrusions.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency and IT/developer users in the US and Europe
incidents.vector: Russian-speaking actor uses ClickFix lures and trojanized software installers (MobaXterm, WebEx, Zoom, DBeaver, FACEIT) to deploy a Python-based 'Starland RAT' and a PowerShell C2 implant.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos detailed a financially motivated campaign (UAT-11795) active since June 2025 that steals browser credentials and cryptocurrency wallets and can deliver follow-on payloads including CastleStealer and Remcos RAT, with most victims in the US.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited the platform's own price-reporting (oracle) infrastructure.
incidents.impact: The Ostium DeFi platform was drained of roughly $18 million.

incidents.vector: Reportedly compromised following infection by the Shai-Hulud npm worm; internal files and source code were dumped online.
incidents.impact: A threat actor leaked Suno's source code and internal documents, allegedly exposing large-scale scraping of songs and lyrics from YouTube Music, Deezer and Genius.

incidents.vector: A GitHub Actions 'pwn request' exposed the asyncapi-bot token, letting the attacker publish five poisoned package versions carrying an import-time 'Miasma' loader through the project's trusted publishing pipeline.
incidents.impact: Microsoft found the compromised @asyncapi/specs and generator packages execute at module-load time (bypassing --ignore-scripts), fetching a second-stage payload with C2, persistence and disabled credential-harvesting modules that affected developer workstations, CI/CD and container builds.

incidents.victim: Windows enterprise users (global BEC phishing targets)
incidents.vector: BEC emails impersonating FedEx and other shippers deliver obfuscated JavaScript and a Lua/AutoIT loader disguised as a TrueType font file for fileless, in-memory execution.
incidents.impact: Fortinet's 'TFF Trap' campaign deploys RATs and infostealers (Agent Tesla, Remcos, XWorm, Best Private Logger) with low detection rates to steal data and take control of Windows systems.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659 and CVE-2026-56164 for unauthenticated RCE, followed by theft of IIS machine keys and deserialization for persistence.
incidents.impact: CISA warned of active exploitation of all supported on-prem SharePoint versions to gain unauthorized access, steal machine keys and deploy malware; the three CVEs are in CISA's KEV catalog and hardening/AMSI guidance was issued.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure network devices (Five Eyes and allied nations)
incidents.vector: FSB Center 16 actors scan for internet-exposed routers with default or weak SNMP community strings and use SNMP/TFTP (plus occasional Cisco CVEs and Smart Install) to exfiltrate device configurations.
incidents.impact: A joint advisory from NSA, CISA, FBI and 12+ allied agencies warned that Russia's FSB Center 16 continues to opportunistically compromise poorly configured routers across energy, government, telecom, defense, financial and healthcare sectors for espionage.

incidents.vector: Voice phishing to trick staff into authorizing malicious OAuth apps, plus supply-chain compromise of Salesloft Drift, Gainsight and Klue integrations and abuse of misconfigured Salesforce guest/Aura access.
incidents.impact: Microsoft detailed ShinyHunters-associated campaigns (mid-2025 to mid-2026) abusing trusted OAuth relationships to enumerate and mass-exfiltrate CRM records across many tenants without triggering conventional sign-in anomalies.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-Service affiliates use edge-device exploits, brute force, stolen credentials and custom tooling (Go/C encryptors, a 'GentleKiller' EDR killer) to breach and encrypt victims.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 reports 'The Gentlemen' RaaS has claimed 580 victims across 77 countries since mid-2025, becoming 2026's second most active ransomware program with a roughly 6x jump in victims and an unusually high 90% affiliate payout.

incidents.vector: Actors scan for and exploit known vulnerabilities in WordPress and other CMS plugins (unauthenticated upload, RCE, SSRF, deserialization) to deploy webshells.
incidents.impact: Australia's ACSC warned of a large-scale global campaign deploying webshells via roughly 17 CMS/plugin CVEs, enabling defacement, credential capture, malware hosting and broader network compromise, with many Australian small and medium businesses impacted.

incidents.victim: Edge routers and IoT devices (operational relay-box network)
incidents.vector: Exploits n-day flaws in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers to deploy custom Linux backdoors (LONGLEASH, DOGLEASH, JARLEASH) and build operational relay-box networks.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos reports the China-nexus actor (UAT-7810) continues expanding the LapDogs ORB network with new malware, providing covert infrastructure used by other Chinese state-linked groups to attack high-value targets.
